newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon wins $512 mln U.S. Army contract.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon wins $512 mln U.S. Army contract.

text.p: Raytheon Co said Wednesday it won a $512 million contract from the U.S. Army to build and operate a chemical weapons destruction plant in Pine Bluff, Ark.

Raytheon said its engineering and construction firm Raytheon Engineers and Constructors will provide the project's overall management, construction, equipment procurement, start-up, operations and maintenance, and ultimately closure of the facility.
The company said the Pine Bluff arsenal, set up in 1941, covers nearly 15,000 acres and stores 12 percent of the 30,500 tons U.S. chemical weapons stockpile.

Rayteon in February received a $567 million U.S. Army contract to build and operate a similar facility in Umatilla, Ore. It added it received a $500 million contract in September 1996 to keep on operating the army's Johnston Atoll Chemical Agent Destruction System facility in the Pacific.
The company's stock traded at 56-1/8 Wednesday afternoon, up 7/16 and close to its 52-week high of 56-9/16.
